narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook, in order of importance, were your total years of professional experience, the length of time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (1–5 years is most common among stayers), your mid-range experience level matched patterns the model associates with people who eventually move on. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your current organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction, as this tenure is typical of those who start looking elsewhere once they have gained some familiarity with the company. Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities during your time here further increased the likelihood of departure, since external offers often signal that an employee is actively considering or being recruited for new roles.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model sees as likely to exit. You and your manager may want to discuss ways to strengthen your sense of long-term fit and explore internal growth paths that could reduce the pull of outside opportunities.
